# HStackedWaveform

> Dense, centered waveform pillars built from ordered colored amounts with subpixel segment gaps.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.9.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HStackedWaveform` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-stacked-waveform>`.
- Constructor: `HearthStackedWaveformElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HStackedWaveform.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Each column is a centered stack of ordered segments, read top to bottom. Repeated colors/labels remain separate segments: use unique segment ids within each column and stable column ids. Values are amounts, not normalized percentages. Total pillar height is proportional to its sum on a shared scale set by the largest visible total.
- The 0.5px default gap separates colored pieces. Gaps are deducted from the pillar height before distributing fill by amount; tiny pillars reduce gaps to retain proportions. segmentGap is clamped to 0–0.9px. Zero, negative and nonfinite amounts have no fill and appear as zero in the data table.
- Bars default to 8px with 3px column gaps; the row stays dense and centered like HWaveform, shrinking to fit narrow containers. height is bounded to 44–320px, barWidth to 2–12px, columnGap to 0–8px. The latest maxPoints columns are shown (default/maximum 128).
- One native range input covers the whole plot for keyboard and touch inspection without widening individual pillars. Hover inspects; arrows/Home/End and touch dragging use native range behavior. change commits select(id); selected is application-owned. Tooltips and a data-table disclosure expose totals and every ordered segment; no per-frame live announcements.
- Use tone for theme-aware colors, or color for trusted application-authored CSS colors. Updated amounts transition under normal motion; reduced-motion changes are immediate. There is no illustrative autoplay because the heights encode actual data. Overflowing numeric totals are marked Above numeric range while individual finite amounts remain available.

## Public API

columns: StackedWaveformColumn[] · label, description, selected, unit: string · height: number = 96 · barWidth: number = 8 · columnGap: number = 3 · segmentGap: number = 0.5 · maxPoints: number = 128

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    columns: StackedWaveformColumn[];
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    selected?: string;
    height?: number;
    barWidth?: number;
    columnGap?: number;
    segmentGap?: number;
    maxPoints?: number;
    unit?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    columns: () => [],
    height: 96,
    barWidth: 8,
    columnGap: 3,
    segmentGap: 0.5,
    maxPoints: 128,
    unit: "",
  }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, title, plot, pillar, segment, control, tooltip, data, empty

Use `hearth-stacked-waveform::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface StackedWaveformColumn {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    segments: WaveformSegment[];
}

export interface WaveformSegment {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    value: number;
    tone?: Tone;
    color?: string;
}

export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HStackedWaveform } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const columns = [{id:'one',label:'Pillar 1',segments:[{id:'green',label:'Green',value:1,tone:'success' as const},{id:'red',label:'Red',value:10,tone:'danger' as const},{id:'blue',label:'Blue',value:5,tone:'info' as const}]},{id:'two',label:'Pillar 2',segments:[{id:'green',label:'Green',value:2,tone:'success' as const},{id:'red',label:'Red',value:12,tone:'danger' as const},{id:'blue',label:'Blue',value:7,tone:'info' as const}]},{id:'three',label:'Pillar 3',segments:[{id:'green-top',label:'Green',value:5,tone:'success' as const},{id:'red',label:'Red',value:12,tone:'danger' as const},{id:'green-bottom',label:'Green',value:12,tone:'success' as const}]}];
</script>

<template>
  <HStackedWaveform label="Stacked amounts" :columns="columns" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-stacked-waveform');
Object.assign(element, {
```

## Related components

- [HWaveform](../waveform/llms.txt): A lightweight signal visualization with CSS motion, pause control, and reduced-motion support.
- [HStackedBarChart](../stacked-bar-chart/llms.txt): Normalized percentage columns for changing multi-series data, built from HTML spans.
- [HDivergingBarChart](../diverging-bar-chart/llms.txt): Slender percentage bars above and below zero, with a fixed ±100% scale and exact-value inspection.
